newsitem.title: GHANA: Fresh Ghana VAT bid two years after bloody riots.
newsitem.headline: Fresh Ghana VAT bid two years after bloody riots.

text.p: Ghana's government asked parliament on Wednesday to reintroduce Value Added Tax (VAT) two years after bloody riots led to the withdrawal of the levy.
A memorandum with the bill or draft law said that the tax, if passed, would be one of the most effective and equitable in the West African former British colony.
The draft proposed a 15 percent levy on a range of goods and services from January 1998 compared to a 17.5 percent levy which was withdrawn in July 1995.
It would replace sales and service taxes.
President Jerry Rawlings's government introduced VAT in February 1995, sparking popular protests. Clashes between government supporters and opponents killed five people in May 1995.
Rawlings won reelection in December and his party won a healthy majority in parliament.
Under the bill, VAT would apply to all goods and services originating within Ghana and imports and imported services, other than those specifically exempted.
Exemptions range from mining, farm, industrial, dredging and rail equipment to livestock, medical supplies, oil and oil products and domestic electricity up to a certain amount.
